clue.text: River Test is used for manufacturing

parts.note: the Indus, the great river of Pakistan

explanation.surface: A report on an English river being put to industrial use.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'River Test' look like the Hampshire trout stream; the two words have to be split, the river being a different one entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the adjective for factories, plant and production lines, things used for making goods.

clue.text: Reverse vehicle in front of a line of ships

indicators.note: tells you to turn the vehicle back to front
puts the reversed vehicle before the rest

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A driver backing a vehicle up to the head of a queue of ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A line of ships' reads as a convoy, but the definition is only 'of ships'; 'a line' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval means of or relating to ships and a navy.

parts.note: a Tory is on the political right

explanation.surface: A political claim that a staunch Conservative is a person of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Tory' reads as one phrase for a traditionalist Conservative; it splits into two pieces. Tory is the nickname of Britain's (and Canada's) Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: standing straight becomes morally straight, as in a citizen of good character.

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so a word is heard rather than read

parts.note: also = too, heard rather than spelt

explanation.surface: Two people who also happen to be chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a couple talking together, when the talking is the signal to listen to 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a pair is the number that comes after one.

definitions.meaning: verb sense: to set up, as proceedings or a rule
noun sense: a college or learned society

explanation.surface: An instruction to found a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as verb and object, but each is a definition on its own: one verb, one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Institute is both a verb meaning establish and a noun for an academy.

clue.text: Rent out fields before close of June

indicators.note: puts the fields ahead of the next piece

parts.note: leas are meadows, a poetic word for fields

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A farmer letting out pasture ahead of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: LEA (a meadow) is an old poetic word that crosswords use constantly for a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a landlord grants a tenancy of a flat or farm for rent.

clue.text: Material in child's bed not turned back

indicators.note: tells you to write NOT backwards

parts.note: a cot is a baby's bed (a crib)

explanation.surface: Worry over which fabric sheet goes in a baby's crib, left unfolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' looks like part of the instruction, but it is the word to be turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fabric woven from the fluffy fibre of a plant.

indicators.note: the answer is inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A spy overstating what a secret file contains.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap between 'undercover' and 'document'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to take something too far, laying it on thick.

indicators.note: puts A and D inside the show

parts.note: an exhibition = a SHOW, opened up
A plus D, the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A notice describing a one-day show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outline' reads as a verb meaning summarise; the answer is a silhouette.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow is a dark outline cast by an object.

definitions.meaning: verb: to mark something out for attention
noun: a flat slab of stone used for paving

explanation.surface: Pointing out a feature stone in a patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highlight' reads as a noun, the best bit; it is the verb, to pick out for notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag means both to mark for attention and a flat paving slab.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone finds a liqueur oddly stored among the teacups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the liqueur inside the tea set; it is two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sweet French aniseed-flavoured drink.

clue.text: A river had stripped stump in botanical garden

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
had = bore, as in bore a child

indicators.note: a stripped word has lost its outer letters

parts.note: sTUMp without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stream that has worn a tree stump bare in a botanic garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' is the past of bear in the sense of giving birth or carrying: she bore/had twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a botanical garden given over to trees, from Latin arbor, tree.

clue.text: Outdoor bath and barrel put back behind house

indicators.note: tells you to write BUTT backwards
places the barrel after the house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a butt is a large cask; BUTT reversed

explanation.surface: Setting up a bath and an old barrel out behind the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' tempts TUB directly, which is almost right; the barrel is a BUTT, and turning it gives the second T.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated bath kept outdoors.

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple: bent into a new shape

explanation.surface: Shop owners making a shortage worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun (goods) but is the adverb from supple, pronounced SUP-lee: nimbly, so the letters bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: those who hold title to a shop, hotel or other property.

clue.text: Regularly query fellow calling for immediate action

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter of query is kept

parts.note: q U e R y, the even letters

explanation.surface: A man who keeps asking questions because he needs things done now.
explanation.walkthrough: GENT is the crossword's usual fellow; 'Regularly' here keeps the second and fourth letters of query.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: pressing, needing attention right now.

clue.text: Cooking areas close to long passageways

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Kitchens sited near long corridors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near; here it means the close, the last letter, of 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the kitchen on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: The world of dancing in revues

indicators.note: dancers change places across the stage, so the letters of in revues swap positions

explanation.surface: The glamorous world of stage revues and their dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' again looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, the whole world.

indicators.note: the letters are put together afresh
drop R, the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Antonín Dvořák writing music without any spirit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' is exactly what Dvořák did, which hides its job as the rearranging instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a clear distilled liquor from Russia and Poland.

clue.text: Fast starts to laps ensure notable times

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A runner's quick laps guaranteeing good times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is read as speedy, fitting the running; it is the noun, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter.

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French city putting up a visiting English relative.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the Riviera resort; the surface reads the English relative as a houseguest, when the E is simply the abbreviation for English.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a brother's or sister's daughter is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Believe in fragment of sacred item

indicators.note: the answer is a piece of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of sacred and the start of item

explanation.surface: Faith placed in a splinter of a holy relic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Believe in' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Believe', and 'in' links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to accept a claim as true or trust a report.

explanation.surface: Discreetly asking for a favour.
explanation.walkthrough: P for quietly comes from piano in musical scores; 'favour' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb, to like best.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to like one option better than the others.

definitions.meaning: to slate or savage, as a reviewer does a flop
a metal vessel for frying or boiling

explanation.surface: Complaining about a kitchen utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses share a word by chance: a reviewer who pans a show has nothing to do with the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan means both to criticise harshly and a cooking vessel.

explanation.surface: A woman minister handling a parish's publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: AD is short for advertisement; a minister leads a Protestant congregation, and the clue's clergywoman is simply one who happens to be a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to run the affairs of an estate, office or department.
